Host lifecycle, hello, and macOS/Windows/Linux no-flag app sessions are implemented; full named-role and privileged dispatch remain absent.

WKWebView, WebView2, and WebKitGTK backends plus the common verified profile foundation exist; Windows signed-package identity and profile lifecycle checks have real-device evidence. A same-origin five-store isolation matrix passes across signed apps and publishers and an existing second ordinary user, including restart, first-user retention, and cleanup. Full Windows profile acceptance, macOS/Linux authenticated producers and persistent stores, the destination engine policy, and the renderer bridge remain incomplete.

kipc framing, codecs, HELLO authentication, Unix bootstrap, and the Windows named-pipe app-link are implemented; KEL-270 T4d S4a adds the Windows keld-attempt endpoint (#510): the exact `\\.\pipe\keld-attempt-<64 lowercase hex>` name shape, an initiating-user-only connect-back pipe with closed descriptor forms checked through one shared reader and comparison, and a client that requires the server's session, with authentication id, elevation and elevation type added to the peer token facts. KEL-270 T4d S4b adds the keld-attempt claim and health record codec (#602) on the owner-approved wire text: AH1, AC1, AA1/AR1, AB1, AY1, AF1 and AK1 with magic-first, position-admitted reads, the transcript and AB1 binding checks (KELD-IPC-014 to KELD-IPC-017) and an attempt_records fuzz target, plus the Windows-only purpose-1 BLAKE3 connect-back locator, which shares one prefix constant with the endpoint name check. KEL-270 T4d S6a runs the exchange inside the endpoint and client (#607): the claim (AH1, AC1, AA1, AR1) and health (AB1, AY1, AF1, AK1) sequences run in `WindowsAttemptEndpoint` and `WindowsAttemptClient`, which never expose the stream; the endpoint derives its name from the IDs its AC1 carries, a refusal re-arms the same instance and consumes no one-shot, and the owner's health window is a pure state machine with an injected clock whose late entry fails closed (KELD-IPC-018 to KELD-IPC-021). The S4b record codec is now crate-private behind a doc-hidden fuzzing hook. No production caller composes the exchange yet: the composition in keld-core and keld-host and the measured G constant are S6c (open), the bootstrap records and purpose-2 locator are absent (S11), and nothing in activation or the helper uses the exchange. Channel registry and shared-memory lanes are absent.

Manifest parsing, evaluation, verified startup loading, and guard-before-handler dispatch exist, as does the single KEL-135 Windows Authenticode verifier (KEL-270 T4d S8; keld-core calls it, and the embedded identity is read through its verified handle by KEL-254 T3 Part B, #390). KEL-270 T4d S7 adds safe Windows wrappers for the Machine-UAC helper (#511): the initiating token (opened from the host process by borrow, one primary and one impersonation duplicate, a scoped impersonation that reverts on return, error and unwind), a Medium non-elevated token profile check, own-token session and `SeImpersonatePrivilege` checks, and logon-session time and ended checks through `LsaGetLogonSessionData`. S4a adds the shared ACE-equality rule used by the keld-attempt pipe checks (#510). Nothing calls the S7 wrappers yet (S11 and S12 consume them; the S9c helper calls only the S8 Authenticode verifier) and their two elevated-token operator rows are unrun; generated grants and audit logging remain target behavior.

The retained filesystem broker is implemented with verified-snapshot binding, guard-selected retained scopes, bounded no-follow traversal and regular-file I/O. Native Windows and Linux rows on exact landed ancestor `d22e454...` are publicly reported in [PR #262](https://github.com/gyldlab/keld/pull/262), while the final three-OS terminal artifact is authenticated in private Linear only and therefore is not yet a public proof surface. No production host caller is wired, and the other planned native services are absent.

Single-child supervision, crash accounting, macOS guardians, Windows primary generations, and Linux strict preparation for the no-flag primary exist; KEL-270 T4d S5 adds Windows connect-back claimant binding (#389): the retained launch object keeps the suspended child and its creation time, and a claimant binds only if its process handle compares equal to it (`CompareObjectHandles`, only TRUE matches), the launch is still running, and its process ID and creation time equal the recorded launch. KEL-270 T4d S9b adds the elevated-helper primitives (#606): `restrict_dll_search_to_system32` (SetDefaultDllDirectories with LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_SYSTEM32, KELD-RUNTIME-018) and `launch_elevated_updater_helper` (ShellExecuteExW `runas` on a dedicated STA COM thread, no owner window, over a drive-letter .exe path type and a closed argument type, KELD-RUNTIME-019); the repository owner's non-elevated-parent UAC consent and decline rows passed at that head, and the launch has no production caller until S11. KEL-270 T4d S6b adds the PerUserDirect same-token candidate launch (#618): a CREATE_SUSPENDED child through the generalized suspended-child type, `assign_child` returning an unforgeable `WindowsJobMembership` proof that `resume` requires (a bare same-token resume is refused and the previous suspend count must be exactly 1), a launch liveness check and the proof's creation time read before the Job admits the host (KELD-RUNTIME-020). The S5 claimant binding and the S6b launch are not wired into activation: the composition is S6c (open), and the pipe, token, deadline and one-shot cells of the claimant-binding row remain open (S6c, S11). Full named-role and remaining product strict admission remain absent.

Windows x64 fixed-NTFS packages support actual-SYSTEM machine-baseline initialization/admission, an explicit-UAC MachineUacDirect baseline initializer (an elevated operator run seeds the common baseline and a filtered token refuses before any write), and a native PerUserDirect baseline/bootstrap primitive under the installing user's owner-private profile. The per-user initializer seeds a verified immutable baseline, stable activation lease, floor/current/LKG and provenance-last commit. Ordinary-token no-UAC, real LPAC mutation denial and 11 baseline crash cuts pass. Native Windows updater tests also prove higher-release extraction and completion of an immutable stage under the retained writer lease; the completed stage is neither published nor selected and active records/journal stay unchanged. KEL-270 T4b adds the common journaled PerUserDirect transaction: activation, exact receipt binding, commit/rollback, version retirement, recovery from every persisted cut (62 native crash cuts) and the explicit unjournaled-version repair for orphans left by the earlier order. KEL-270 F1 journals each attempt before renaming its stage to the version name, re-verifies the candidate before the floor moves and abandons an attempt whose stage is gone. KEL-270 F3a adds read-only active package selection for ordinary startup (KEL-254 AC4): a shared-lease snapshot that refuses a pending journal as journal-bound and a lease sharing conflict as WriterActive, requires current to be a known-good artifact within the floor, admits only referenced versions with metadata admission and the signed no-migration package policy, and pins the selected tree and its protected ancestry; 15 native tests and 7 mutation controls. KEL-270 F3b adds the startup repair: an absent or undecodable current is republished from a re-validated last-known-good under the PerUserDirect writer lease (6 mutation controls); a decoded current is never rewritten. KEL-254 T2b adds executable-located selection: the build-time ExpectedAppIdentity is decoded and matched field-exactly against the located provenance record before that same handle is admitted against the recorded mode's profile; every recorded root must be the located root by volume serial and file ID on the record's volume, the executable handle must be the selected tree's keld-host.exe, and current is repaired only for the last-known-good host (12 native per-user tests and an independent security review); machine-mode and non-NTFS selector cells remain operator rows. KEL-254 T3 Part B adds ExpectedAppIdentity::from_signed_image, which reads the embedded expectation through keld-pack's handle reader from the image KEL-135 just verified and applies decode's channel and key admission (container and read refusals are KELD-UPDATE-019; payload refusals stay KELD-UPDATE-017); the KEL-96 host now consumes executable-located selection. KEL-270 T4d S2 adds a typed Machine-UAC recovery-required startup state (#385): an ordinary startup of a MachineUacDirect installation that finds a pending journal, or an absent or undecodable current beside a valid last-known-good, returns `ActivationEffect::MachineRecoveryRequired` with closed guidance text and writes nothing, using the same read-only last-known-good validation as the per-user repair; `RecoveryDisabled` is the only value production can produce until the helper's recovery-only role (S10, S12) exists, and the owner's elevated Machine-UAC operator run of this state passed at the merge head. KEL-270 T4d S3 moves the activation journal to `keld.activation-journal/v2` (#509): each record carries the initiating logon (authentication id and logon time) and the attempt owner (process id and creation time), a zero logon id is refused by encoder and decoder, and `begin_activation`, `resume_unlaunched` and `recover` return a minted attempt that has written nothing until its `journal()` call; the owner process id is supplied by the caller, not observed. KEL-270 T4d S9a (#608) adds the helper image to the located installation: a closed WindowsLocatedImage choice (host or updater helper) replaces the fixed host constant, `anchor_updater_helper` self-anchors the helper to its installation and the activation role derives the helper image, a helper locator never repairs current, and the signer rule (the protected record's publisher scope and app id equal to the verified identity) moves from keld-core into keld-update, now running before the snapshot lease and any per-user current repair (KELD-WV-009 becomes KELD-UPDATE-020; helper refusals KELD-UPDATE-021). KEL-270 T4d S6b adds the owner and claimant primitives (#618): the claimant's lease-less provenance read (`locate_candidate_claimant`), criterion 20's authenticated candidate-boot read (`read_candidate_boot`, every refusal a typed WriterActive) returning the AB1 health-receipt digest, the owner's expected digest accessor, and `accept_health` split into a durable `HealthAccepted` step and `complete()` (breaking, must_use). None of this is composed into a production path: the S4b locator takes its minted attempt and health-channel IDs as input, the owner process id is supplied by the caller, and S6c (composition) is open. T4d overall is not complete: S1 is deferred; S6c, S6d and S10 to S12 are open (S6a, S6b and S9a to S9c have landed). The helper's recovery role stays disabled until S10, no production caller composes the connect-back until S6c, and an owner lost mid-health is unrecoverable until S6d. Candidate selection, installer integration, host candidate launch and 30-second health, feed orchestration and the machine modes remain absent.

Windows hosts can stream canonical Windows v0 tar/zstd update packages with the fixed no-migration policy and byte-domain size/BLAKE3 receipts; other hosts refuse production before I/O. It also owns the canonical build-time ExpectedAppIdentity payload codec (KEL-254 T2b): a domain-tagged app id, channel, target and Ed25519 update key with fixed bounds, no control characters and exact EOF, pinned by a golden vector; KEL-19 T1 adds the host container (#386): a pure writer embeds the payload as a dedicated `.keldeai` PE section of the unsigned host before its final signature, and a positioned-read reader over a byte slice (every target) or an open Windows file handle shares one stack-bounded structure parser; the reader authenticates nothing, so a result is authentic only when read from the handle KEL-135 has just verified. The KEL-254 T3 Part B host consumer reads the container at boot through keld-update's from_signed_image; KEL-19 T2 adds the Windows acceptance rows (#515): an embedded but unsigned release host is refused with KELD-WV-009 and WinVerifyTrust 0x800b0100 before any listener, child or window, and a once-signed image fails the KEL-135 verifier with 0x80096010 when a payload, padding or section-size byte covered by the Authenticode hash is flipped while an excluded CheckSum byte still verifies; these are ignored operator rows with a hash-chained receipt, run on one Windows 11 machine, and the KEL-135 verifier still accepts an image with a second, unauthenticated WIN_CERTIFICATE entry, which only the T2 single-entry test assert catches; the owner assigned the single-entry check to the KEL-19 T3 AC11 post-sign check. KEL-270 T4d S9a (#608) makes the helper a required package member: canonical Windows v0 content requires exactly one root regular-file `keld-updater-helper.exe` (the producer refuses before any I/O, the verifier decides after the content digest, and the golden fixture was regenerated), and the container error texts (KELD-PACK-005 to KELD-PACK-012) name either image. KEL-19 T3 (`keld build` integration) remains absent. Installers, signing, notarization, CLI build integration and cross-host assembly remain absent.
Compatibility evidence types, scoring, and lifecycle conformance exist; broad Electron host emulation is absent.
The shipping host owns hello and macOS/Windows/Linux no-flag sessions; the destination registry and release packaging remain absent.
create emits the checked-in Rust-derived echo payload declarations; dev, doctor, MCP, hello, and IPC diagnostics exist, while build, migrate, gen, and ext remain reserved.

The elevated updater helper keld-updater-helper.exe is specified by KEL-53 §4 "Helper launch and self-anchor". KEL-270 T4d S9c adds its binary crate (#619): a per-binary static C runtime with System32-only import resolution, main's first statement the System32-only DLL search, the one-argument check (exactly one exact keld-attempt rendezvous or the exact `--recovery-role` selector, decided before any open and never echoed), and one KEL-135 verification of its own image that feeds keld-update's self-anchor (KELD-HELPER-001 to KELD-HELPER-004). Both roles still refuse after a passing self-anchor: the activation role until S11 and the recovery role until S10, so the helper performs no activation, recovery or write. A release-build CI step checks the PE import allowlist and KEL-19 AC1 and AC2 on the release helper. No Machine-UAC operator acceptance of the helper anchor exists yet, and the running-image binding before S10 and S11 add a write path is an open owner decision.
The Electron facade implements lifecycle and the app-link client; the wider Electron module surface is absent.
The canonical TypeScript app-link transport is live, and bounded cold tooling derives checked-in echo payload declarations from the Rust structs; general schema codegen and bulk lanes remain absent.
The typed SDK for supervised Bun roles is specified but no package is tracked.
The renderer bridge and polyfill package are specified but no package is tracked.
The npm binary resolver is specified but no package is tracked.
The contract-definition and code-generation package is specified but no package is tracked.
The package-manager scaffolding entrypoint is specified but no package is tracked.
The tracked workspace, architecture, agent workflow, and CI exist; the first attributed performance harness remains absent.
macOS, Windows, and Linux no-flag app sessions exist; the full public role API and release artifact chain remain absent.
MCP v1, permission evaluation, guard dispatch, one filesystem broker, and bounded echo declaration generation exist; bulk IPC, general schema codegen, and broad compatibility remain absent.
The Linux strict mechanism is implemented and consumed by the no-flag primary; distribution, signed updates, remaining OS/profile admission, limits, reporting, and addon workers remain incomplete.
Compatibility-depth, corpus, pinned-engine, and stable-plugin goals are specified but not implemented.

The shipping app-link uses a current-user protected named pipe plus HELLO; distinct ordinary-user denial and authorized same-user successor echo are proven, while decimal diagnostic compatibility remains.
The no-flag host, native window, app link, recovery, and ordered cleanup are implemented for the current slice.

The no-flag host, native window, named-pipe app link, recovery, ordered cleanup, and authenticated Authenticode identity-to-persistent-WebView2 wiring are implemented; the single KEL-135 Windows Authenticode verifier is owned by keld-guard (KEL-270 T4d S8) and keld-core calls it. Windows admits two boot states (KEL-254 A3 AC2): a dev lease reaches only the owner-private dev-stage validator, and a lease-less launch boots only the authenticated installed package (KEL-254 T3 Part B). keld-core verifies the executable once, reads its embedded ExpectedAppIdentity from that pinned handle (KELD-UPDATE-019/017), selects the installation through KEL-53's executable-located entrypoint (KELD-UPDATE-*), requires the protected record's publisher scope and app id to equal the verified identity through keld-update's signer rule, which runs inside that selection before the snapshot lease (KELD-UPDATE-020, moved from keld-core's KELD-WV-009 by KEL-270 T4d S9a) and opens the strict boot files beneath the selected tree, all before any listener, child or window; the persistent profile comes from that boot identity. On 2026-10-06 the KEL-135 signed rows passed on fresh per-run PerUserDirect installations of P1/P2-signed embedded hosts built from this slice (RAMANI, unelevated): startup, which also shows that the running session pins its version directory, profile concurrency, crash release, the five-store App A/B/other-publisher isolation matrix and both purge rows, with signed refusals for a host without a container, one outside an installation, one under another recorded publisher and one signed for another app. These are native rows of the installed route, not KEL-254 installed-boot acceptance: KEL-19 T2's AC2 and AC8 rows have since passed as operator rows (#515; one Windows 11 machine), but KEL-19 T3 (`keld build` integration and its post-sign check) and KEL-254 T4 are open, machine-mode installed boot is reachable but unqualified, and the second ordinary user's row, machine-mode installed cells and updated, rolled-back or candidate boot (KEL-254 T4) remain unrun. Earlier dev-stage evidence covers the second ordinary user's store isolation, restart, cleanup, and first-user retention; filesystem denial; and saved-media grant revocation. Broader Windows profile acceptance and all macOS/Linux browser-profile acceptance remain incomplete.

The no-flag host, WebKitGTK window, authenticated app link, strict Bun generations, recovery, CLI/host-death cleanup, and relaunch are implemented for Ubuntu/Debian x86_64 Wayland; X11, non-Debian, and release packaging remain unverified.
